newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end down in robust trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end down in robust trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed down on Tuesday as investors took a more defensive stance following recent gains, but finished well off the day's lows as some buyers continued to cautiously pick up laggards, brokers said.

"I think there has been some cautious buying during this period of consolidation," said Gary Wong, associate director at Vickers Ballas. "The futures have been trading at an 120-point premium to the index for the past two days. I think that is a positive sign."
The Hang Seng Index shed 61.30 points to close at 13,456.26 after trading at a low of 13,422.10. Turnover was a vigorous HK$7.2 billion, roughly in line with Monday's HK$7.38 billion.

Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was much less active than last week, with only 12,579 contracts traded. The December contract closed down 25 points at 13,580, but at a 120-point premium to the spot market. The January contract lost 30 points to 13,630.

Utilities, which have tended to lag the overall market's recent gains, were the only sector to buck the downtrend. The commercial and industrial sector led the market down, followed closely by the property sector.
Laggard Hongkong Electric put on HK$0.65 to HK$25.75 and China Light gained HK$0.30 to HK$33.70, while HongKong Telecom lost HK$0.05 to HK$13.50.
Brokers said China Light covered warrants had also seen good demand and rising premiums in the past two days.
New World Development was the day's worst performing blue chip, with a fall of HK$1.25 to HK$51.50. the share had risen more than 10 percent in November.
Cheung Kong, which was the day's most active share, finished down HK$0.50 at HK$69.00.
Among the conglomerates Swire Pacific gained HK$1.00 while Wharf Holdings slid HK$0.80 and Wheelock slipped HK$0.50 to HK$21.80.
The H share index maintained the gains of the morning to close the day up 2.28 percent at 834.81. The sector is getting a boost from positive sentiment in the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets.
Tsingtao Brewery led the sector, putting on HK$0.10, or 4.3 percent, HK$2.725, followed by Northeast Electrical which gained HK$0.07 to HK$1.10.
Meanwhile, the Shanghai A index rose to a high of 1,237.03, then eased 16 points to close down at 1,178.61. The index has risen more than 2,000 points in the past two weeks.
